notes.title: ROADMAP
notes.notes: [p]First, apologize to veteran players; past communication about the entire development plan was indeed insufficient.  [/p][p]From now on, we will improve this.  [/p][p]The main nodes of future development plans, as well as completed ones, are published and recorded here.  [/p][p][/p][p]We hope players can set clear and realistic expectations for this game's development.[/p][p]We may make minor adjustments during development based on feedback from community.[/p][p]However, the overall development direction will not change.[/p][p][/p][p]At least from my own experience, I've never encountered such gameplay mechanics.[/p][p][b]Additionally, while this incorporates many findings from sociological research, it also includes a lot of my personal bias and subjective input.[/b][/p][p][b]Mistakes are inevitable in the process, and we sincerely ask for your understanding.[/b][/p][p][b]I offer my deepest gratitude in advance to all willing to dive in.[/b][/p][p][/p][p][i]Please note that this only covers key development objectives; many minor features and details will be presented in the game itself during development and will be detailed in development logs.[/i][/p][p][/p][h1]Overall Goal: Social Shaping/Construction  [/h1][h3]Social Shaping:  [/h3][p]Use external violent competition as a major factor influencing social structure  [/p][p]- gives players a survival/competition goal, so they know what to do;  [/p][p][/p][p]Then use "male-female/gender relations," patriarchal/matriarchal/equal rights/matrilineal, etc., possible gender relations as the basis of social rules  [/p][p]- players can choose which basic gender relation to adopt as the foundation, forming class-family and other social structures;  [/p][p][/p][p]Then use various classical political philosophy concepts as ways to mediate social contradictions  [/p][p]- players can choose which concepts to use to regulate social contradictions;  [/p][p][/p][p]Ultimately achieve the gameplay of freely shaping society according to players' ideals or in-game goals.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h1]2026 - Class  [/h1][h2](Design Completed) Patriarchal Society -> Family  [/h2][p]Increase in male social status: Achieve noble status through merits in various battles, diplomacy, and internal management  [/p][p]Men possess women, simultaneously creating demand: property needed for women to bear and raise offspring.[/p][p align="start"]This will give rise to private ownership. The more women possessed, the greater the demand for property.[/p][p align="start"]Women, once possessed, enter patriarchal families, and players will also lose direct operational control over women.[/p][p align="start"]Women's social functions will depend on their husbands,[/p][p align="start"]For example, the wife of a leader, besides doing housework, will also participate in labor with her husband;[/p][p align="start"]The wife of a noble does not participate in labor, devoting herself to education, culture.[/p][p align="start"]Overall, women will primarily engage in "supporting husbands and raising children," providing numerical bonuses to their husbands and children in education/social status.[/p][p][/p][h3](Design in Progress) Matriarchal Society  [/h3][p]Historically, and even today, it exists.  [/p][p]Historically, it can only exist in environments with less intense competition. For example, certain relatively isolated mountainous areas, plateaus, etc.  [/p][p]In the game, we are considering granting unique cultures, diplomacy, victory methods, etc., to maintain playability balance.  [/p][p][/p][h3](Design in Progress) Various civilizations outside China  [/h3][p][/p][p][/p][h1]2025 - Worldview, External Factors of Society  [/h1][h2](Starting Soon) Morale[/h2][p align="start"]We already have a team system and leaders.[/p][p align="start"]The morale system will introduce strategies such as "demoralizing the enemy" in combat, while also imposing limitations where the number of people a leader can command depends on their social status and leadership.[/p][p align="start"]This is important groundwork for the emergence of the class-family society. Social status and leadership can be enhanced through class, official positions, and family education.[/p][p][/p][h2](Completed August) Reduce Female Attack Power  [/h2][p]Reducing female attack power makes the division of roles between genders more pronounced.[/p][p]Women manage reproduction, while men possess greater combat strength.[/p][p]Introducing this mechanic lays important groundwork for the later emergence of class-based and family-centered societies.[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1876880/view/530982192097001483"][/dynamiclink][/p][h2](In Production) Continue optimizing overall experience[/h2][p]Refining diplomacy system, animal allocation, room construction management, tutorials, performance, etc.[/p][p][/p][h2](Completed July) Group marriage [/h2][p]Design basis: Consanguine family, intermarriage within the same generation, such as collective marriage among siblings, children do not know who their father is.  [/p][p]Note: This is not matriarchal society. The matriarchal society option has not yet been added to the game.  [/p][h2](Completed July) Framework of the worldview:  [/h2][p][/p][p]This is the detailed explanation for this:[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1876880/view/530976484112729252?l=english"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]The internal structure of society is usually significantly influenced by external pressures/factors.  [/p][p]Violent competition is mainstream. Thus, male status inevitably rises.  [/p][p][/p][p]Design adopted main reference materials:  [/p][p][i]"The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State"  [/i][/p][p][i]Author: Friedrich Engels  [/i][/p][p][i]Core chapters: Chapter 2 "The Family" (Section 2 "The Family") & Chapter 3 "The Iroquois Clan" (end part)  [/i][/p][p][i]Work: "Women, Production and Patriarchy in Pre-industrial Societies"  [/i][/p][p][i]Author: Diana G. Coontz (1983)  [/i][/p][p][i]Chapter: Chapter 3 "The Military Revolution and the Domestication of Women"  [/i][/p][p][i]Work: "The Warrior Society: How War Created Patriarchy"  [/i][/p][p][i]Author: Ruth Eisentadt (2021) Core chapter: Chapter 4 "The Weaponization of Inheritance: Bronze Age Europe" (pp. 112-145)  [/i][/p][p][i]Work: "Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind"  [/i][/p][p][i]Author: Yuval Noah Harari  [/i][/p][p][/p][h1]2024 - Colony Build as Foundation [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680212/7ca6ee426ef6911c6b94a8abf818aac4082a8a3a.png"][/img][/h1]

notes.title: Response: Support & Criticism for the New Version
notes.notes:
[p]‌Recently, some friends who preferred the previous version have contributed to an increase in lower ratings.[/p][p][/p][p]I too enjoyed the relaxed experience of the old version. Unfortunately, its gameplay had reached a developmental dead end.
The art overhaul stems from these reasons:[/p][olist][*][p]Aligning with the new thematic direction. Without showcasing the world's brutal competition, gameplay would stagnate. My focus is societal evolution—remaining a casual builder contradicts this vision.[/p][/*][*][p]Previous art, while detailed, compromised clarity for controls and interactions.[/p][/*][*][p]It also caused performance issues during late-game scaling.[/p][/*][*][p]Facial/hair/clothing diversity will return—currently delayed due to workload.[/p][/*][/olist][p]To those dissatisfied with our direction: I regret any communication gaps. I shared development visuals and beta explanations, but clearly fell short. My sincere apologies.[/p][p]This update demanded extraordinary effort. By March 2024 (launch month), I recognized the old design's ceiling. Some team members began prototyping this new version then, while maintaining old updates until October 2024—despite steadily declining player counts and sales. Minor optimizations couldn't revive stagnant gameplay.[/p][p]The conclusion is undeniable: the old path led nowhere.[/p][p][/p][p]The new version is now playable.
Player counts, sales, and reception have surged dramatically these past days. I'm grateful to the team members who persevered. ‌The team has even welcomed new members.[/p][p]We'll press forward—hoping supporters of this vision stay with us.[/p][p][/p][p]P.S. Group marriage remains current. Family trees and kinship systems will reemerge as core mechanics, evolving the game into the era of familial invention.[/p][p]

notes.title: Design Philosophy Behind the Worldview & Cultures of Other Nations
notes.notes:
[h1][b]A World of Competition[/b][/h1][p]
This reflects my core values as the creator.
War is a significant catalyst for societal change. Note I say "catalyst," not "driving force."
War—or more precisely, "competition"—has propelled much of human civilization's development. Note I say "development," not "progress."[/p][p]Personally, I dislike war, yet it remains an objective factor in social evolution. Our goal is to "shape societies," which inherently involves change—thus competition must exist.
The need for sustenance (food) and security (safe rest)
necessitates empowering the strong.
This concentrates labor, energy, attention, respect, and resources in the hands of the few (elites) or even individuals (heroes).
Thereafter emerge class systems, patronage, exploitation, ownership, and rule.
Hence the need for morality and laws to mediate class conflicts.
Moreover, even these aren't exhaustive reasons. As development progresses, I'll selectively implement gameplay around impactful elements.[/p][p][/p][h1][b]Resulting Gameplay[/b][/h1][p]
Without competition, the sense of purpose weakens—severely hindering strategic choices and gameplay expansion.
Currently, you can experience:[/p][list][*][p]Boosting fertility through fertility cults[/p][/*][*][p]Enhancing combat via warrior worship[/p][/*][*][p]Increasing productivity through slavery[/p][/*][*][p]Shaping influence by mythmaking
These are foundational methods to "shape society," forming the implemented core gameplay.[/p][/*][/list][p]We wholeheartedly welcome constructive critiques.[/p][p][/p][h1][b]Playable Factions[/b][/h1][p]
Current factions center on ancient China. After framework refinement, global cultures will emerge.
This is the primary purpose of the Culture Tree mechanic.
We're considering Mycenae (proto-Greek), Babylon, and Egypt—undecided as yet.
While Greek/Spartan culture and philosophy are renowned,
Babylon's historical period aligns better with our setting—but our cultural understanding remains insufficient, requiring further research.[/p]

notes.title: On the design goals, and future development directions.
notes.notes: [p]Based on feedback from the current beta, some players have been deeply engaged, while others have expressed a preference for the more relaxed tribe-building experience of the previous version.[/p][p]It’s important to clarify our design goals and communicate them in detail to help set appropriate expectations.[/p][h2]Competitive Worldview[/h2][p]The current version presents a relatively harsh worldview. However, note the "Culture Tree." We will build on this foundation to introduce more "idealistic" societal paths—such as a peace-oriented matriarchal society—offering a more leisurely experience. These options must remain grounded in historical plausibility. While the previous version was relaxed, it diverged too significantly from history. For human civilization, conflicts and warfare have been the norm.  [/p][p]Recent numerical adjustments also prioritize "competition" as the core metric. Certain mechanics—like cooking speed or livestock feed rates—may feel slower than before, but as long as they strategically enable outpacing rival factions, they serve their purpose.  [/p][p]That said, I fully agree that excessive perceived sluggishness diminishes enjoyment. I’ll continue refining these elements holistically.  [/p][p]Beyond Micromanagement[/p][p]With "competition" as the driving force, excessively micromanaging individual labor assignments shouldn’t burden players as "rulers of the world." While the current labor interface offers some production control, its impact is intentionally limited.  [/p][h2]Diverse Societies, Diverse Experiences[/h2][p]The previous version forced passive defense, with content auto-unlocking through knowledge. Meaningful strategic choices were scarce—minor production tweaks (crops vs. livestock) yielded negligible differences, and activities like clothing production required livestock with no alternatives.  [/p][p]The new version establishes a historically grounded foundation with real choices. We’ll expand upon this to deliver richer strategies and experiences. If the current build isn’t to your taste, please be patient—societies aligning with your values (like peaceful matriarchies) are coming.  [/p][p]I fully respect diverse playstyle preferences. My plan is to introduce these alternate experiences via distinct nations/cultural/political doctrines, shaping societies that match player desires.  [/p][p][/p][h2]Current Core Gameplay Loop[/h2][p]Strategic now focus lies in diplomacy and schedule. [/p][p]And like other grand strategy games, the gameplay cycle:[/p][p]1) Achieve victory (unify the region) through one strategy.[/p][p]2) Replay with varied approaches—examples include:[/p][p]   > Early war[/p][p]   > Cultural indoctrination[/p][p]   > Trade dominance[/p][p]   > Slavery systems[/p][p]   > Tributary networks[/p][p]   > Military conscription[/p][p]---[/p][p]Leaders & Future Development[/p][p]Leaders currently function as "grouping" tools for management. Later, they will evolve into "nobility," introducing social classes. I’ll detail this in future videos and announcements.  [/p][p]---[/p][p]A Work in Progress[/p][p]This project is highly experimental, constantly evolving through exploration. Your feedback is invaluable. Please continue offering your constructive criticism!  [/p][p][/p]

notes.title: NEW BETA AVAILABLE - UPDATE 0.3 IS AT THE BETA BRANCH NOW
notes.notes:
[h1]Hello Great Leaders![/h1][p][/p][h3]It is finally time for some news, we are working on it for several months, thank you for your patience so far![/h3][h3][/h3][h3]First part of the post we will give some explanations of the direction of the game and later we will present the new good stuff![/h3][p][/p][h1]Sim Colony x Grand Strategy[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680212/a4b38ccda4e5be31ed9bff63daf93aaf488d4d3c.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680212/f38c63c97b0d16f2afae6603d96f70271fb3ff3b.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680212/c6eeb52d0ce4410d3484c17487bab31daa172f5c.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43680212/abcc800ea56443acbd1f5463de0e32bf1637b9e3.png"][/img][/p][h2]This isn't a Traditional Sim Colony:[/h2][p][/p][p]The Traditional Ones might be focused on "survival", with a lot of natural disasters and surviving rounds of bugs, zombies, or invaders or it can be about logistics management, space planning, building pipes, conveyor belts, waterways, etc., in order to efficiently move goods around and expand production.[/p][p][/p][h2]Primitive Society Simulator will be a "Building Society":[/h2][p][/p][p]We have currently incorporated "competition with other peoples," essentially merging grand strategy gameplay with "map coloring" mechanics.
Players must prevail in this fiercely competitive world.[/p][p]We hope our friends maintain realistic expectations regarding our development progress. We will gradually create a work centered on shaping and building society within the context of human conflict.[/p][p]Management remains a crucial cornerstone – you must develop your tribe effectively, then exert influence over neighboring tribes, turning them into vassals to achieve greater expansion.
Here, war will serve as an extension of politics, though not the sole method; cultural propagation and trade are equally viable paths.[/p][p][/p][p]This game is not the traditional way of playing colony building, and that competition, i.e. war, diplomacy, commerce and trade will be very important, and that just building on your own in silence will not win you the game.[/p][p][/p][h1][b]Important Differences Compared To The Old Version:[/b][/h1][p][/p][h2]1. It's now impossible to directly unlock technology through labor accumulation[/h2][p][/p][p]This old mechanic can lead to players not being able to make choices on technology development. It is very detrimental to the playstyle.[/p][p]I like the old mechanic myself, but it's a temporary compromise for the sake of smooth gameplay and the more important leader system, so I hope you understand.[/p][p]The mechanism now is that the leader creates the technology by leading the crowd, working together, and gathering the wisdom of all.[/p][p][b]Knowledge remains an important factor, and with insufficient knowledge, technology creation will be slow beyond the medium term.[/b][/p][p]The engraving of monuments and the passing on of knowledge is still alive and well and remains a more important play.[/p][p]We will also continue to design better ways to play to reflect the importance of knowledge. Keep up the playstyle exploration of this factor.[/p][p][/p][h2]2. New art style[/h2][p][/p][p]The detail (texture) is reduced. On the one hand this is better for post performance.[/p][p]On the other hand, I think being able to clearly see what people are doing is very important for this work.[/p][p]The characters have become more slender than in the past, and the movements are more realistic, especially the fighting ones.[/p][p]There's still a lot of room for improvements, but the overall presentation of the art style is much more appropriate for this game than in the past.[/p][p]Scenery details will be further enriched by adding buildable facilities.[/p][p][/p][h2]3. Some other removed features:[/h2][list][*][p]Mission, Founding, Oracle. It will be replaced later by a richer system of diplomacy and events.[/p][/*][*][p]Terrain modification. Shouldn't be done again, huge amount of work, other games do it more.[/p][/*][*][p]But the mound of dirt and the altar are still there. They are now used for cultural outreach.[/p][/*][*][p]The "Smoothing Point" is removed, and the need for "emotional pacification" is gone. Now there's no more being scared to death out of fear.[/p][/*][*][p]There are no specialized medical beds. After receiving a lot of feedback from you, we're finally bringing our first [b]Big Update[/b]. Here we're setting a [u]new tone for how we'll be approaching the game's UI[/u], as well as looking to [u]solve the problems related to the gaming pace[/u].

At the end of this post you can find more about the [u]frequency of our future updates[/u].

We've prepared a very simple video to show you some of the changes we've made. The video is also on our new YouTube channel. Previously our posts were made on our personal accounts (sorry about that). By subscribing there, you'll be kept up to date with all the latest news on the game.

Here is the video and right below you will find the description of the changes we've made:

[previewyoutube=-SOnukSUeyE;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Notion of Time[/h3]
[list]
[*] The exact time is not visible now, only the seasons.
[*] The exact time will be unlocked later through the concept of creating time.
[/list]
[h3]UI Style[/h3]
[list]
[*] The UI now has a new, still relatively simple style.
[*] Changes will continue to be made in this area.
[/list]
[h3]Life Expectancy[/h3]
[list]
[*] It used to start with 8 people, but this number has increased to 10.
[*] Your people will live faster, it means, they will age faster and die faster.
[/list]
[h3]The Diurnal Cycle[/h3]
[list]
[*] The days are longer now: From 20 seconds to 30 seconds an hour.
[*] They used to sleep about 7 hours, now they sleep only 5 hours.
[/list]
[h3]Interaction Optimization[/h3]
[list]
[*] The expedition team now automatically calculates the food required. No more doing the math yourself every time.
[*] A new master and apprentice management interface. You don't have to go from one to the other to click on the master at a later stage.
[/list]
[h3]Rhythm of Technological Invention[/h3]
[list]
[*] Farmland on tech tree, moved from level 4, forward to level 3
[*] Wooden Plow on tech tree, moved from level 5, forward to level 4
[*] Brown millet also moved back one level.
[/list]
[h3]Late Years Gameplay[/h3]
[list]
[*] The urgency and manpower needed to help other tribes was increased.
[*] The invasions became more frequent in the later stages.
[/list]
[h3]Compatibility[/h3]
[list]
[*] Most archives will be fine.
[*] Some may face compatibility problems, so you have two options:
[olist]
[*] Restart the game. Enjoy and try all the available modifications right from the start.
[*] Contact us (Discord, Steam Discussions) to see if anything can be done in your specific case.
[/olist][/list]
[u][b]The overall pace of the game seems to have doubled.[/b][/u]

This is how we are going to be working from now on:

[b][Small Updates][/b] Bug fixes, performance optimization: [u]1~2 times per week.[/u]
[b][Updates][/b] Interaction optimization, new features with small changes: [u]once every 2~4 weeks.[/u]
[b][Big Updates][/b] Changes to greater play: [u]once every 4~6 months.[/u]

-YSH Mr. Octopus

notes.title: WHAT'S NEXT?
notes.notes:
[h3]More Maps and RoadMap:[/h3]

We're dealing with a number of urgent matters, as I mentioned earlier, [u]so we won't be able to bring you a RoadMap until June.[/u] Until then, we'll be making these constant small updates, as well as keeping you informed of any news. We are also aware of the need for new maps, which is also a very important topic for us. However, it may be more complex to implement a definitive solution (procedural maps), so we appreciate your patience during the wait (we know it might be longer than some would like to wait).

[h3]Historic or Fiction:[/h3]

Now we have a topic that we know divides many:
[olist]
[*] This game will be historic.
[*] The developers are going to venture into dinosaurs with humans and other more fictional themes.
[/olist]
The truth is that we intend to satisfy everyone. PSS will be focused on its development towards updates with historical content, but we understand that some want to have options to diversify the fun, so in the future (at least 2 years down the line), [u]we will be making dinosaur-related content available through free DLC[/u], so that everyone can enjoy the game in the way that pleases them most, [b]without the game losing its essence.[/b]

[h3]Feedback, Discussions and Analysis:[/h3]

As you have decided to trust a project that is still in development, we believe that as well as believing in our work, you also want to be part of the history of the development of "Primitive Society Simulator".

With that in mind, [u]don't hesitate to share your suggestions both on our Discord server and in the Steam Discussions area[/u]. By the way, we would like to thank every member of the community who has been extremely supportive and helpful, helping to answer various questions made by other less experienced players, [b]you are amazing[/b]. We're reading everything, and it may take us a while to respond due to the various tasks we have to do, so your help is really important.

Finally, we would like to thank each and every one of you who has already reviewed the game, and we will try to honor your trust. This is a long-term project, we have a lot of ambition and we know it's going to be a long road. [u]Reading your reviews every day helps us to see that we have an incredible community waiting for the results of our work[/u], [b]and that's very motivating![/b]

[i]That's all for now,
Feel free to share your opinion about this post in the comments.[/i]

-YSH Mr. Octopus

I've made a post about the future plans, it's pinned in the Discussions, however we'll be drawing up a RoadMap in the coming weeks, but to help you even more in deciding whether to buy the game now or not, [u]I've made a short guide orienting you according to the expectations of each type of player[/u] (remembering that everything is according to the [b]content currently available[/b], more content will come in the coming months):

[b]If you're a builder:[/b] I fit the bill here, you'll probably be able to play for around 100 hours, among the hundreds of players who helped us test the game in its development until now, many even exceeded the 200 hour mark. So I feel that builders can already buy the game without hesitation.

[b]If you're a warrior:[/b] Currently, there are mechanics for morale, building towers, medical support, cleaning the battlefield and preparing weapons. However, compared to more elaborate RTS games such as the "Age of Empires" franchise, several features, such as unit formation, are still lacking. The combat aspect of our game will continue to improve, but not in the short term. So if that's your focus, I think it's worth waiting a little longer.

[b]If you're a productivity fanatic:[/b] It's worth considering the purchase. The structure for weight management, trading systems, transportation and storage areas is ready. Various details are currently being perfected.

[b]If you're a farm game enthusiast:[/b] As it's the time when humans started farming, there are gameplay elements such as "crop selection", "divine agriculture" and "domestication of oxen (aurochs)" based on history, and there are also mammoths to add to the fun. So it's worth giving it a go.

[b]If you're the casual type:[/b] Reaching all the content can take around 50 hours. However, if you don't like building and production efficiency, then it may be a waste of time. You might want to check the reviews before making a decision.

[h3]It's also worth talking about AI, a very important factor in games like ours:[/h3]

Currently, AI's division of labor is quite detailed, which can seem a bit cumbersome at first. However, the resulting control capacity and level of automation are greater. After playing, if you feel that the AI is failing in any respect, let us know and we'll continue to improve it.

[h3]The UI also deserves a special mention:[/h3]

Some people have said that it looks a bit rustic. Objectively speaking, that's true. The point is that the interface of this type of game is very complex and currently, the priority is to make it "understandable and clear". We also tried to improve the style of the interface, but found it difficult to maintain clarity. We'll try more improvements again when the system and gameplay are more stable. If you care about this, please give us some time.

[h3]About the Updates:[/h3]

Various optimizations and bug fixes will continue constantly. Soon, as I mentioned earlier, we'll be making a RoadMap available to briefly show our development plan. Significant new game mechanics will be tested in around 3 months and polished over the same period of time, so released in around 6 months. This cycle may seem a little long, but it allows us to deliver stable updates and significant new content that will offer you dozens more hours of fun.

So if, knowing all this, you decide to embark on this journey with us, we'd be honored and we'll demonstrate this by being as transparent as possible and following up on all the feedback you've left in a variety of places: Discussions, comments on updates, our [b]Discord[/b] ([url=store.steampowered.com] https://discord.gg/uKYW2Ha4fg [/url]) and very importantly we will be reading and taking into consideration all the reviews you leave, if we can ask you something, please as soon as you are comfortable with your opinion of the game, [u]take the time to write your review, it will be extremely important to us[/u].

Now to finish this mega text, we would like to thank all of you who have trusted our work so far, especially the hundreds of content creators who have already made a video in several languages: Arabic, Chinese, Czech, English, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Thai, Turkish and Vietnamese. All of them were not paid to give their opinion, so they were free to give as much criticism as possible, so once again we thank each and every one of them, and you might go and search for their content at: Youtube, Twitch, TikTok and several other places, in that way maybe they could help you to see more about the game and make a clear decision about buying the game now or waiting a bit longer.

PS. The game is available in Chinese, English, French, German, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian and Spanish. But during the EA process we will add more languages.

-YSH Mr. Octopus

notes.title: FUTURE PLANS & PRICING
notes.notes:
[h1]Hello Dear Primitives,[/h1]

[h3](BIG text but a quite important one to read before you buy our game.)[/h3]

We're very grateful for the support of each and every one of you, whether it's helping us find the bugs we've so lovingly created, following our page and putting 'Primitive Society Simulator' on your wishlist or even helping to promote us in your circle of friends and, in the case of content creators, with your own communities. So now it's time to reveal our post-launch Early Access plans and answer many questions that may have arisen over time. Without further ado, let's get down to business.

[h2]What were our inspirations for creating 'Primitive Society Simulator'?[/h2]

We've been working on this project for more than 3 years, and at that time the games that most inspired us were: 'Rimworld', from which we used various terms and some similarities such as the global map, thus making it easier to understand our game for those who are already familiar with the genre; also 'Dawn of Men', when we chose to create a game from this period, we couldn't ignore a title that at the time was perhaps the biggest reference of that era, we were even jealous of their name, hahaha.

[h2]Why 'Primitive Society Simulator'?[/h2]

Over the last few weeks, we've noticed that many people, with good intentions, have questioned why we chose such a name, and that perhaps we should consider changing it. We really appreciate your concern and caring!

According to what you'll read in the following topics, you'll notice that our similarities with the games mentioned above will start to reduce drastically, because we'll no longer be a colony simulator, but a society simulator set in primitive times. Apart from that, what we can say for now is that we are really ambitious to bring something innovative to all of you, and this is the name that made the most sense in view of our ambitions.

[h2]What do we currently have available and plan to add?[/h2]

[h3]Animals:[/h3]
We love animals, whether in real life or in games, but we also understand that many people think that the more variety the better. We want that too, but we can't just add animals because they're cute and flashy, each one needs to play an important role in the game.
At the moment we have, for example:
[list]
[*] Chickens that serve as a good source of food right from the start;
[*] Sheep that provide us with material for our basic clothing and, of course, another source of food too, as all the other animals;
[*] Boars that help us on our expeditions;
[*] Sabretooth tigers which, as well as being our mounts, are also great in our offensives to defend our territory;
[*] Mammoths which help us with the loads, as well as providing precious material for our armor;
[/list]
We have a few other animals that we'll leave for you to discover on your own, but it's important that you know that each animal has its role.

We had already started to introduce dinosaurs, but we weren't satisfied with the results of the mechanics implemented in them, so we removed them for the time being. However, rest assured that we will be adding dinosaurs in the future, as well as other extinct animals, such as the beloved dodo. And to finish off this subtopic, we certainly haven't forgotten about aquatic life, but we'll reveal more about that in the future.

[h3]Relationships:[/h3]
This is where everything starts to stand out, we're very fond of this part and we've noticed that you like it too, for example the feedback about the dialogues around the Bonfire are being very positive and we plan to improve these dialogues even more throughout the game's development period. We hope to add some smiles in you faces while reading those conversations.

[h3]Discoveries and Knowledge:[/h3]
We are very pleased with your feedback on this subject, as it is called in many games the 'Research Tree' or 'Tech Tree'. Here, knowledge is not global, as each individual needs to learn from a mentor, who has learned from another mentor or practicing the activity that led to their discovery. With these mechanics, the following scenarios are possible:
[list]
[*] All knowledge in any area can be lost if the last person who had that knowledge passes away and nothing has been recorded for posterity.
[*] A family can specialize in a particular activity, such as hunting, and thus become the hunting clan of their society.
[*] Each new generation will be able to take advantage of the knowledge left by their ancestors and set off on new discoveries, just as happened in our history.
[/list]
More discoveries will be added with time, we plan to explore this age as much as it is possible. It means for you, more game mechanics, more buildings and more everything!!

[h3]Maps:[/h3]
On this subject, we understand that there may be some frustration and we need to be honest about the current situation. We really only have one map on which to build our settlement, but that's because we're preparing the ground for future development, such as new biomes. Yes, we want to add deserts, forests, tundra and all sorts of other biomes, but that will take time. With this in mind, we will be working on having the option of procedural maps with the resources currently available.

As for the world map, we want to turn it into something more interactive that isn't just limited to data displayed on an interface. In the future, we want to make it possible to invade and explore other territories, as well as more interactive mechanics. Something that already happens to some extent when you encounter wild animals on the world map, but even that we want to improve as well.

[h3]Personalities:[/h3]
This is the main topic so that everything we've talked about makes sense and so that all future plans become a reality. We want to have a society simulator in our hands, and since a society is made up of individuals, we need to design our individuals very well. We start by working on this, as we mentioned previously when talking about knowledge and discoveries. However, that's not all; each individual needs to have their own personality and preferences, which will reflect on their own history and help shape their society.

Let's make this more palatable by using an example:
[list]
[*] Mentors can shout at theirs apprentices: 'If you're always the last one, you will be the food for wolves'. Or them can encourage saying: 'To make it this far, you're even stronger than the oxen in the field!'. Those actions will result in these children developing 'experiences' that will make them either more confident or more timid. And them will gradually grow into either timid ordinary people or great leaders.
[/list]
As you can imagine, our priority will be to implement this mechanic over the next few months. It will certainly be a big challenge, but we're sure it will be worth the effort. This is likely to be the time of greatest instability during the Early Access process, and we will be relying heavily on your support during this stage, so that we can hunt down the bugs, provide the correct balancing and undoubtedly provide good times for you all while playing our game.

[h3]Buildings:[/h3]
When you start a game, sheds are the only protection you can offer to your people, but other forms of free construction are already available within the game and for that you have:
[list]
[*] Wall;
[*] Fence;
[*] City wall;
[*] Stairs;
[*] Door;
[*] Floor;
[*] Roof;
[*] Bridge;
[*] and more.
[/list]
You will also find dozens of useful furnitures and structures, such as:
[list]
[*] Bench;
[*] Pen to feed your animals;
[*] Farmland;
[*] Bonfire;
[*] Food rack;
[*] Defense platform;
[*] War drum;
[*] Patient bed;
[*] and much more.
[/list]
However you will need to advance your knowledge in this area so that everything is available to your people.

[h3]Other Features:[/h3]
We also have more things that we want you to discover by yourselves. Like the health mechanics, events, quests and more.

[h2]Is the game complex?[/h2]

It's certainly not recommended to open the game for the first time and skip the tutorial, even if you're already familiar with the genre, because as we mentioned earlier, we've added unique mechanics to the game that are worth checking out in the tutorial on how to deal with them.

We have some very didactic tutorials, which are constantly being improved. Although the game may daunt some at first due to its high complexity, we guarantee that every effort has been made to ensure that the learning curve is in itself satisfactory and that the feeling of mastering each area of the game is also a source of satisfaction.

[h2]How can you provide feedback?[/h2]

We love to hear/read your feedback even if we can't answer each of them on the right platforms, no matter where you can provide it, be it in the most diverse places such as:
[list]
[*] Youtube, Twitch and Billibilli videos/streams;
[*] Youtube, Twitch and Billibilli comments, yes we are reading what you write over there (at least as much as it's possible);
[*] Steam community;
[*] Your comments in each of our posts at Steam;
[*] One of the best way to do it, at our Discord server;
[*] Another great way is when a bug happen and in-game you can send the report;
[/list]
Just adding an extra, when a bug happens to you, please contact us at the Discord and with the save file, that will help us to find and fix the bug faster. Resulting in a better experience for you all.

[h2]In which languages will the game be available?[/h2]

Our intention is to make the experience of playing 'Primitive Society Simulator' as global as possible, for now the game is available in 6 languages and another 2 are in progress, totaling 8 languages available on the day of release in Early Access, they are:
[list]
[*] Brazilian Portuguese - work in progress
[*] Chinese
[*] English
[*] European Spanish - work in progress
[*] French
[*] German
[*] Japanese
[*] Russian
[/list]
However, as we are doing this with the work of professionals, we can't translate into every language, so we have to give preference to the languages where we have the biggest audience:
[olist]
[*] The easiest way is for you to put the game on your wishlist as soon as possible;
[*] Another way is for you to engage with the content made by the content creators in your language;
[*] Finally, by purchasing the game when it is available for sale. We know that some people won't buy the game until it is available in their language, and we respect that;
[/olist]
We've already decided that we're going to translate the game into other languages during the Early Access process, so at least 2 or 3 new languages will be available by the time version 1.0 arrives. We will still be working constantly to improve the languages already translated.

Finally, we may also have the option of enlisting the help of the community to translate the game into less popular languages. To do this, look us up on Discord, so we can work together to make this possible.

[h2]When will the game be available and how long will it be in Early Access?[/h2]

Previously we posted that the game would be available on February 26th, but we hadn't provided the information regarding the exact time and in which time zone. Forgive us for this oversight, here is the full information on the exact moment when 'Primitive Society Simulator' will be available for purchase on Steam:
[list]
[*] February 26th, 05:00 p.m. PST
[*] February 26th, 10:00 p.m. GMT-3
[*] February 27th, 01:00 a.m. GMT
[*] February 27th, 10:00 a.m. GMT+9
[/list]
We plan to keep the game in Early Access for 2 years, but we won't set a date, because until we're satisfied with the final product, we won't be able to release thr version 1.0, even if the 2-year deadline has passed. So rest assured that we will only leave Early Access when the game is really ready for it.

[h2]How much will it cost?[/h2]

We've studied the market prices very carefully to decide on the price for each country (at least those we can specify), and we can say that we've decided on a price below even Steam's recommendation, because we want as many people as possible to have access to the game as soon as it becomes available. Here are the prices in some regions:
[list]
[*] $19.99
[*] 18,49 €
[*] 599 ₽
[*] R$ 40,00
[*] ¥ 76
[/list]
In addition to this, we'll also have a 10% discount during the first days of launch.

[h2]Any other questions?[/h2]

If you have any further questions, please don't hesitate to contact us via the community area here on Steam or on our [b]Discord[/b] server, which can be accessed by inviting us via the following link: [url=store.steampowered.com] https://discord.gg/uKYW2Ha4fg [/url]

-YSH BigDove Team

notes.title: beta-branch content synchronization to the main branch
notes.notes:
Beta 0.5.0_1204.1301 to 0.5.0_1212.1432 beta-branch content synchronization to the main branch

-------- Improves --------

• Invaders spawned in the first 5 years won't have ranged weapons anymore.
• You can now double-click to select all invaders on the screen.
• You can now double-click to select all corpses on the screen.
• You can select corpses by drawing a box around them.
• Loading saves now displays a progress bar.
• In case of loading errors or freezes, a pop-up error message is now shown.
• When searching for a water source for watering, the game finds the nearest source using a path instead of straight-line distance.
• When someone wants to trade, the trade leader stops wandering around.
• When picking up resources from a production point, the game looks for the closest resource to the character instead of the closest resource to the point.
• Different heights provide advantages for attacks.
• If mines are depleted, new resources randomly spawn during the night.
• When switching crop types on a field with growing crops, a confirmation dialog is now displayed.
• Cremation sites can now cremate three bodies simultaneously, reducing cremation time.
• The locust plague interval has been adjusted to occur every 60-90 days.
• Expedition teams now show their path on the world map.
• Crocodile skin price increased from 2800 to 3800, while rhinoceros skin price remains unchanged.
• People can change their surnames and names, animals can be renamed, and newborn babies will automatically take their father's surname.
• Optimized the workload of carrying soil: Soil weight reduced from 10 to 0.1, and soil stack size increased from 50 to 500. An option to disallow soil carrying will be added later. 
• Added animal mating animations for all animals except humans.
• Vertical synchronization option added.
• Added a one-click clear work priorities button.
• Added copy and paste functionality for work priorities.
• Orders for buildings like tool benches can now be copied and pasted.
• When your character dies, all equipment and items will drop.
• Removed flooring generated when digging or building soil.
• When saving and loading games with multiple items in a single storage slot, item quantity counting errors no longer occur.
• Optimized the appeasement refresh mechanism for improved efficiency.
• Bridges are now constructed as a single structure; old bridges will automatically convert to the new design.
• When the sacrificial area is modified, the wealth value is immediately refreshed.


-------- Bug Fixes --------

• Domesticated animals, close to giving birth, taken for hunting can't be controlled and stay in place.
• Winter lasts from Spring 10th to Summer 1st, causing snow to melt and then reaccumulate.
• Items dropped on frozen rivers will be transported to the riverbank when it thaws but remain uncollectible.
• Dismantling an animal pen while animals are grazing may prevent the sheep from returning to the pen.
• Attempting to install a building directly from the backpack results in an error.
• Ghost health bars in farmlands.
• Unfinished stone monuments can still be inscribed.
• Deleting a starting slope by clicking on a building directly removes the building.
• When releasing sheep, if one of the sheep is interacting with someone else, it doesn't get released.
• Errors occur when attempting to wear both raincoats and clothing simultaneously.
• Errors occur in the trade interface when entering non-integer values.
• Errors occur when planning food trough quantities and then dismantling the animal pen.
• When constructing bridges, characters may take a longer path to the other side.
• Characters engaged in carrying items or merging item stacks will eat only after completing their tasks, potentially resulting in starvation.
• If an item required for construction is missing, characters can get stuck; now, the installation will be canceled if the item is missing.
• Multi-selecting buildings sometimes displays buttons for both prioritizing and deprioritizing food gathering. 
• When moving medicine, characters may consume herbs before placing them in storage.
• The background of the work assignment interface is misaligned.
• Tooltips for completed bridges do not display.
• Several bugs related to simultaneous cremation of three bodies in pyres.
• Picking up a single piece of grass and returning it to storage.
• Characters eating at the nearest campfire sometimes choose a caravan campfire.
• If resources are too close together (within 1.5 units), characters cannot start gathering them.
• After trading with a caravan leader, the leader sometimes remains stationary.
• Caravans affected by the above issue may leave the map but have individual members remain after loading a save.
• Loading a save during impending winter and then loading a save without winter still shows the warning in the upper left.
• After delineating/removing a ritual area, the roof becomes permanently displayed.
• After loading a save, the ritual area is hidden but the toggle switch remains visible.
• Pyres now start burning with just one body, and two more can be added after ignition.
• Unfinished drying racks now display numbers.
• Building floors under stairs/defense platforms may cause characters to become stuck.
• Characters may become stuck when their tools have extremely low durability while mining.
• Animal pens without walls may cause animals to go berserk and generate errors.
• Characters may complain about lacking tools during resource gathering without considering their current equipment.
• The "Idle" need may display repeatedly.
• Egg collection ratios have precision issues.
• In some cases, chicken coops may still have uncollectible eggs.
• Jumping from neutral to revered in relations with other tribes may prevent the completion of the "Distant Friends" quest.

notes.title: Primitive Society Simulator Next Fest Demo is here!
notes.notes:
Hi!

You’ve been asking us to make Primitive Society Simulator available to a larger audience. So, how about just letting everyone play? We've just released our first-ever, time-limited demo – just in time for Steam Game Festival starting next week! 🥳

[h1]What's in the demo?[/h1]
[previewyoutube=6eNSOiUAhAU;full][/previewyoutube]
[olist]
[*] Approximately 8 hours of gameplay. The full version offers 40 hours of gameplay.
[*] You can experience basic systems such as gathering, hunting, fishing, farming, herbalism, and combat.
[*] You can raise basic animals like chickens, sheep, dogs, and pigs, but not advanced ones like mammoths or saber-toothed tigers.
[*] You can experience special gameplay mechanics such as inscriptions, reproduction, and education. However, you won't experience the altar and ceremonies, or large-scale warfare systems in the later stages.
[*] You can experience basic logistics tools like animal power and carts, but not the extensive tribal trade and diplomatic relations.
[*] You can build simple shelters, houses, and warehouses. However, the construction system for wonders cannot be experienced.
[*] The process of forming alliance takes about 30 hours, so it won't be experienced either.
[/olist]


[h1]Next Fest Demo availability[/h1]

The demo is available in English and Simplified Chinese.

As we continue preparing for the Early Access, beta testing is still ongoing, and we will continue to maintain and update the Next Fest Demo for a period of time.


[h1]How to play Demo?[/h1]

To download the demo, simply go to Primitive Society Simulator's updated Steam page and click the button at the top of the game's description.

After you have played, share your feedback with us on our Discord, and spread the word!
Add to the wishlist to stay up to date with the latest news and updates!
